title: Hosted API: regional rollout safeguard playbook and automated rollback tooling
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Summary: Define and implement a tested, automated safeguard playbook for Hosted API regional rollouts that reduces blast radius and enables deterministic rollbacks. Deliverables: 1) a canonical rollout playbook (runbook) that combines blue/green cutover, progressive traffic tapering (attenuation curves), and SLO-driven gating; 2) automation to enact attenuation curves and instant circuit-breaker rollbacks via the orchestrator; 3) observability hooks and dashboards to make gating decisions actionable; 4) a post-incident checklist and a DR rehearsal plan.

Background: We continue to see subtle regressions surface only at regional scale during fast rollouts (latency spikes, 5xx bursts tied to model variant memory behavior, or upstream rate-limiter thrash). Current manual tactics (manual weight changes + Slack coordination) are slow and error-prone for multi-region blue/green swaps. This ticket hardens the pipeline so rollouts are reproducible, reversible, and constrained by SLO/health signals.

Goals: - Reduce mean time to rollback from minutes of manual coordination to < 90s automated action (trigger + rollback). - Limit customer impact by enforcing an initial stagger window and automated attenuation curve (e.g., 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with safety holdpoints). - Ensure rollouts respect per-route token-latency and error-budget thresholds; if threshold crossed, hold and/or rollback. - Provide a runbook and automation that can be run for Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private (config flags for environment differences).

Acceptance criteria: - Playbook doc in Confluence linked from ticket and Console Runbooks section. - Orchestrator accepts an attenuation profile and regional schedule and performs the weight shifts automatically. - Two independent gating signals implemented: (a) SLO-based (p90 latency > configured threshold or error-rate > configured threshold) and (b) resource-based (GPU utilization / mem pressure exceeding setpoint). - Automatic rollback executes a safe drain and traffic rehoming with no more than 10% request loss over a 5m window in canary/initial stages. - End-to-end integration test that simulates failures and validates automation triggers a rollback. - Dashboard tiles in Console for rollout progress, per-region health, and per-route SLOs.

Implementation notes: - Attenuation curves are parameterized objects: initial_percentage, step_multiplier, max_step, hold_minutes. The orchestrator will at runtime compute ramp steps and schedule weight shifts. - Rollback semantics: when a gate trips, the controller first attempts a tapered drain back to the previous active set (blue) with prioritized draining for warm KV-cache sessions; if drain fails due to resource pressure, escalate to immediate regional failover to previous model variant. - Health signals are aggregated at 10s cadence with 3-window exponential backoff for noisy signals. Gate evaluation uses a sliding-window error budget that factors in traffic weight to avoid overreacting to low-volume noise. - Integrations: Console (dashboards + approval UI), Tracing service (link traces to rollout tiles), PagerDuty + Slack for escalations, and GitHub for audit (rollout automation posts PR/commit refs).

Testing plan: - Unit tests for attenuation logic. - Integration test harness that can replay recorded workload traces and emulate regional degradation (latency/error injection). - Chaos test: synthetic 5xx burst injected during a staged rollout to assert hold and rollback. - DR rehearsal: simulate cross-region outage and validate automated failover.

Runbook highlights (linked artifacts below): - Pre-rollout checklist: validate model artifact hashes, probing endpoints, baseline SLO snapshot, and smoke test on a canary route. - During rollout: monitor the rollout tile, watchgate timers, and console approval prompt (if manual hold enabled). - On gate trip: follow automated rollback steps; if automation cannot complete within 90s, engage manual oncall with the emergency rollback play. - Post-rollback: collect logs, capture heap/memory profile, annotate PRs and release notes, schedule postmortem if customer impact > low.

Risk/Tradeoffs: - More aggressive automation reduces time-to-rollback but increases chance of incorrect rollbacks due to false-positive signals; mitigations include multi-signal gating and traffic-weight aware thresholds. - Extra orchestration complexity increases surface area; we'll incrementally release automation behind a feature flag and limit to internal canaries first.

Links and artifacts: - Playbook (confluence): https://confluence.internal.redwood.com/display/RUNTIME/Regional+Rollout+Safeguard+Playbook - Design doc (drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1rOLpExampleDesignDoc - Orchestrator PR: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/4123 - Auto-rollback worker PR: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/4187 - Integration tests: https://github.com/redwood/repo/tree/main/integration/rollout-harness - Console dashboard prototype: https://console.internal.redwood.com/dashboards/rollouts/87209 - Incident learning reference: https://wiki.internal.redwood.com/incidents/2025-09-regional-latency
comments: 2026-01-12 - Maya Patel: Created ticket after postmortem for 2025-09 regional latency incident. Initial scope approved by Runtime PM. Proposed attenuation curve parameters and gating signals included in design doc.
2026-01-18 - Liam O'Connor: Spike complete for attenuation algorithm. Implemented scheduler prototype and validated ramp math with synthetic traffic. Results attached to PR #4123.

2026-01-22 - SRE Review (Aisha Rahman): Suggested increasing health-signal aggregation cadence to 10s and adding a second signal for GPU mem high-water. Also recommended feature flagging the automation.

2026-01-29 - QA (Diego Alvarez): Integration harness can simulate 5xx bursts and asserted that automated hold occurs at 20% weight during tests. Noted flakiness when traffic < 0.5% leading to noisy metrics; added traffic-weight threshold check.

2026-02-03 - Security (Priya Nair): Reviewed runbook for audit trail needs. Requested automatic audit entries for each weight shift (GitHub comment + console event). Security review concluded no extra controls required.
2026-02-05 - Liam O'Connor: Implemented basic rollback worker and wiring. Next: add draining prioritization for KV-hot sessions and schedule a rehearsal with Platform team on 2026-02-18.
